To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
NO regulates the activity of the Na-K-2Cl cotransporter and of the Na/H exchanger in the thick ascending limb.
NO modulates the activity of the Na/H exchanger, the Na/K/2CI cotransporter, and the Na/H exchangers in the renal tubules.
NO inhibits the activity of the Na/H exchanger in the proximal tubules and Na/K/2Cltansporter in the TALH and collecting duct.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of NO and other vasoactive substances in the control of renal function.
the role of nitric oxide in the modulation of ion transporters in the mammalian kidney.
the regulation of renal sodium transport by nitric oxide and the role that this regulation plays in the pathophysiology of salt-sensitive hypertension.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NO is a potent inhibitor of Cldependent and Cl-independent Na transporters.
NO is a major modulator of Cl-dependent and Clin-dependent sodium transporters in kidney, but further research is needed to clarify the precise mechanisms involved.
NO is a powerful regulator of renal transporters, and its effects are mediated through the inhibition of NaCl absorption and the stimulation of NaCl excretion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NO is a potent modulator of Cl-dependent transport in the kidney and that NO is an important mediator for the natriuretic and diuretic action of NO in vivo.
NO inhibits NaCl absorption in the proximal tubules, thick ascending limbs of the loops of Henle, macula densa cells and collecting ducts.
NO is a key regulator of sodium and water excretion by the kidney.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NO is an important modulator of sodium reabsorption in the kidney and may have important clinical implications for the treatment of hypertension, edema and heart failure.
NO inhibits the activity of Cl-dependent sodium transporters in various nephron segments, which is consistent with the diuretics and natriuretics effects observed in vivo.
NO modulates Cldependent sodium transport by inhibiting apical and baso-lateral Cl channels and by inhibiting the activity of the Na/K/2C1 cotransporter.
